explanation: Use Kadane’s scan for ordinary intervals. For wrapping intervals, compute maximum prefix sums from each end and combine a prefix ending at or before a split with a suffix strictly after that split.
timeComplexity: O(n): one ordinary scan, two cumulative-maximum scans and one split scan.
spaceComplexity: O(n): the prefix and suffix maximum arrays store one entry per position.
attribution: Adapted reference from epi_judge_python_solutions/maximum_subarray_in_circular_array.py; Elements of Programming Interviews Judge contributors; CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 International, retained in repository LICENSE. Explanation authored for EPI Practice.
correctness: Every interval either is ordinary or crosses the array boundary. A crossing interval is a disjoint prefix and suffix. At each split, the running maxima select the best prefix and suffix allowed on opposite sides; considering all splits therefore covers the best crossing interval without repeating an element. The ordinary scan starts at zero, preserving the permitted empty answer.
walkthrough: For [5,−8,6], ordinary Kadane gives 6. Maximum prefix sums are [5,5,5]; corresponding suffix maxima after each split are [6,6,0]. Combining the first split gives 5+6=11 for wrapped [6,5], which beats 6.
edgeCases: All-negative values return zero because an empty interval is allowed.
Prefix and suffix must lie on opposite sides of the split.
